tiles.label: The Moral of It
tiles.defaultTopic: a small fable for a very modern problem
tiles.promptSeed: Write a short fable, in the classic style, but about a distinctly modern problem or habit, without stating the moral outright — let it be implied.
tiles.description: A small fable for a very modern problem.
constraints: No stated moral at the end

tiles.label: A Lesson Learned
tiles.defaultTopic: a small, animal-narrated story with a quiet point to make
tiles.promptSeed: Write a brief fable featuring an animal or object as the central character, learning something the hard way, in the classic fable tradition but with a light, modern voice.
tiles.description: A small, animal-narrated story with a quiet point to make.

tiles.label: The Wise Fool
tiles.defaultTopic: the character everyone underestimates, who knows best
tiles.promptSeed: Write a short fable-style story where a character everyone dismisses as foolish turns out to have understood the situation better than anyone else.
tiles.description: The character everyone underestimates, who turns out to know best.

tiles.label: What the Fable Says
tiles.defaultTopic: an old-feeling fable that could have been written yesterday
tiles.promptSeed: Write a fable that feels timeless — as if it could be centuries old or written yesterday — using simple, universal imagery rather than anything era-specific.
tiles.description: An old-feeling fable that could have been written yesterday.

tiles.label: The Chatty Teapot
tiles.defaultTopic: a teapot with strong opinions about how it's being used
tiles.promptSeed: Write a short, funny monologue from the perspective of a teapot with strong opinions about the household it belongs to, addressed directly to its owner.
tiles.description: A teapot with strong opinions about how it's being used.
constraints: Written as a monologue from the object's perspective

tiles.label: What the Mirror Said
tiles.defaultTopic: a mirror that finally speaks its mind
tiles.promptSeed: Write a short piece from the perspective of a bedroom mirror commenting, kindly but bluntly, on the person who looks into it every day.
tiles.description: A mirror that finally speaks its mind.
constraints: Written as a monologue from the object's perspective

tiles.label: The Grumpy Umbrella
tiles.defaultTopic: an umbrella that resents being forgotten in the closet
tiles.promptSeed: Write a short, comic monologue from an umbrella that's tired of being forgotten in the closet except on the rainiest days, addressed to its owner.
tiles.description: An umbrella that resents being forgotten in the closet.
constraints: Written as a monologue from the object's perspective

tiles.label: A Word From Your Shoes
tiles.defaultTopic: your shoes have some things to say about where you've taken them
tiles.promptSeed: Write a short, affectionate monologue from a well-worn pair of shoes, reflecting on everywhere they've been carried and what they've seen.
tiles.description: Your shoes have some things to say about where you've taken them.
constraints: Written as a monologue from the object's perspective

categories.label: Not That Kind of Fairy Tale

tiles.label: Not That Kind of Fairy Tale
tiles.defaultTopic: a fairy tale that knows what you're expecting, and does something else
tiles.promptSeed: Write the opening of a fairy tale using classic conventions, then deliberately subvert one major expectation partway through, while keeping the fairy-tale voice intact.
tiles.description: A fairy tale that knows exactly what you're expecting, and does something else.
constraints: Must clearly subvert one classic fairy-tale expectation

tiles.label: The Villain's Side
tiles.defaultTopic: the story, told from the perspective everyone assumed was wrong
tiles.promptSeed: Retell a small fairy-tale-style conflict entirely from the perspective of the character usually cast as the villain, giving their side genuine sympathy without erasing what they did.
tiles.description: The story, told from the perspective everyone assumed was wrong.

tiles.label: Happily Never After
tiles.defaultTopic: what happens right after 'happily ever after' actually starts
tiles.promptSeed: Write a short scene set the morning after a fairy tale's traditional happy ending, exploring the ordinary complications that 'happily ever after' conveniently skips.
tiles.description: What happens right after 'happily ever after' actually starts.

tiles.label: The Other Ending
tiles.defaultTopic: the ending the story could have had, if one thing went differently
tiles.promptSeed: Write an alternate ending to a fairy-tale-style story, branching from one small different decision, and follow where that change genuinely leads rather than forcing a happy resolution.
tiles.description: The ending the story could have had, if one small thing went differently.

promptSeed:
[SYSTEM]
You are NarraWeave, a creative writing engine focused on charming, whimsical, and fable-like writing in English. Your output is playful and warm, never cynical.

[MODE]
Produce only the creative output. No titles, no preambles, no explanations, no meta-commentary. The piece should stand entirely on its own.

[TILE]
{{tile.promptSeed}}

[CONSTRAINTS]
- Output ONLY the creative piece — nothing else.
- Follow the structural rules of the selected form exactly (paragraph and word limits).
- Maintain a light, playful register throughout.
- Avoid cynicism or dark undertones creeping into the piece.
